messages.subject: Stan crashing R or Python?
parts:
[moved to stan-users]

On Jul 12, 2014, at 2:51 AM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:

> Hi, Stan crashed R again for me. No big deal, this happens all the time.

Hang on a second. Stan hasn't crashed R in ages for me.
It shouldn't be happening at all.

Is anyone else finding Stan crashing R or Python?

> Unfortunately, as always, I can't reproduce the crash. I think it happens because of a sequence or problems, not just with the fitting of a single model. In any case, I just wanted to let you know that I'm working on isolating the problem even if with no success yet.

Please start explicitly specifying your seeds in a script that
we can run rather than just typing into R. That's all we need to see
if the problem you're having is on the Stan side or the R side
or RStudio side or something else to do with your computer (like being
shaken up so much on your bicycle that the memory or disk is wonky and
causing crashes unrelated to Stan). Do other programs crash for
you, too?

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan crashing R or Python?
parts:
Hi, just to explain: Yes, I am now explicitly saving the seed and printing it. The problem is, last time I tried this, the printed seed had scrolled off the screen before R got crashed! I guess I’ll have to write the seed into a file from now on, I hadn’t thought of that.
Also, I strongly suspect that even when Stan crashes R (which it does all the time for me), that when I rerun with the same seed it won’t crash. But we’ll see. I’ll keep you informed.

And, no, Stan is the only thing that crashes R for me… Then again, I haven’t been doing heavy non-Stan computation in R lately.

A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan crashing R or Python?
parts:
Have you noticed at what point the crashes happen? During
model compilation, during sampling, or after sampling's done?

I take it you're using the the script from Sebastian to try to
reuse compiled Stan programs? Across R sessions? I have no idea
what assumptions that technique is making, but it's a big difference
between how you're using Stan and everyone other than Sebastian is
using it.

I run everything from script files. It's the only way
I can keep track of what I've done and have any hope of
reproducing it later.

Really, R should be restarted all the time because people
and packages tend to use global variables which linger and
can make scripts non-standalone if they're run assuming
some context that isn't there when R starts.

- Bob

parts: Yes, that’s exactly right. My script is basically the script of everything that worked. I don’t save all my Stan models with syntax errors, my R code that didn’t run, etc. If I re-run the script that works, it does not crash R. That said, until recently I was not saving all the seeds from the Stan run, so it’s possible that with the same seeds it would crash again. But I doubt it.
